nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Heat-related health impacts_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the average increase of air temperatures in Connecticut from 1896 to 2023?
nodes.answer: The distinct average increase of air temperatures in Connecticut was 1.99 degrees Celsius from 1896 to 2023.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Heat-related health impacts_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How many days has the Heat Wave (HW) season in Athens extended per decade since the 1960s?
nodes.answer: The Heat Wave (HW) season in Athens has extended by up to 7 days per decade since the 1960s.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Heat-related health impacts_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What time frame do the trends in Heat Waves (HWs) compare from in the study by Founda et al. (2022)?
nodes.answer: The trends in Heat Waves (HWs) were compared from 1900 to 2019 in the study by Founda et al. (2022).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Heat-related health impacts_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What changes were observed in summer daily minimum air temperature (Tmin) in Athens after the mid-1980s?
nodes.answer: The summer daily minimum air temperature (Tmin) in Athens was found to increase at similar rates to Tmax following the mid-1980s.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Heat-related health impacts_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the expected increase in the number of very hot days by the end of the century under the RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 scenarios?
nodes.answer: The number of very hot days is expected to increase by 20 days under RCP4.5 and by 45 days under RCP8.5.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Heat-related health impacts_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What trend was observed regarding nighttime UHI intensity in the Athens Metropolitan Area?
nodes.answer: An increasing trend of nighttime UHI intensity was observed, predominantly during summer and autumn.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Heat-related health impacts_qna_006
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How intense was SUHI in Athens as reported in the paper?
nodes.answer: The mean intensity of SUHI in Athens was 5.6°C.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Heat-related health impacts_qna_007
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does the climate change impact the population's vulnerability to air pollution in Athens?
nodes.answer: The steadily rising temperatures projected for the Mediterranean region may increase the local population's vulnerability to air pollution, as high temperatures are linked to enhanced formation of air pollutants.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Heat-related health impacts_qna_008
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How have PM2.5 concentrations in Athens been affected during heatwaves in 2021 and 2023?
nodes.answer: During the heatwaves of 2021 and 2023, PM2.5 concentration levels in the city center were enhanced by 30% and 10%, respectively, compared to the average summer value.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Heat-related health impacts_qna_009
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the relevance of WHO's limit of 15 gm 3 in the context of air quality during summer periods?
nodes.answer: The relevance of WHO's limit of 15 gm 3 is that exceedances of this limit appear more frequent and intense during heatwaves, indicating a relationship between temperature extremes and air quality.
